senses.def: the fact of owning something
examples: Home ownership has become harder for young people.
The team changed ownership twice in five years.

senses.def: a feeling of responsibility for a task or project
examples: Good managers encourage employees to take ownership of their work.

senses.def: a gas in the air and water that people, animals and plants need to live
examples: The patient was given oxygen in the ambulance.
Plants release oxygen into the air during the day.

senses.def: the speed at which someone walks or runs, or at which something happens
examples: She walked at a fast pace to catch the bus.
The pace of change in technology is incredible.

senses.def: a single step, or the distance of one step
examples: He took two paces back from the edge.

senses.tr: (sinirle) bir aşağı bir yukarı yürümek, volta atmak
senses.def: to walk up and down a small area, especially because you are nervous
examples: He paced the hallway while waiting for the test results.

note: "Keep pace with" = move or develop at the same speed as (ayak uydurmak).

senses.def: to put clothes and other things into a bag or case for a trip
examples: Have you packed your suitcase yet?
Don't forget to pack a warm jacket.

senses.def: to fill a place with a lot of people or things
examples: Fans packed the stadium for the final game.

senses.def: a set of things wrapped together for sale, or a group of animals that hunt together
examples: She bought a six-pack of soda and a pack of gum.
A pack of wolves was spotted near the town.

note: "Packed" (adjective) = very crowded (tıklım tıklım).

senses.def: something wrapped or put in a box so that it can be sent by mail or carried
examples: A package arrived for you this morning.
The package was left on the front porch.

senses.def: a set of things offered or agreed together as one unit
examples: The government announced a new economic aid package.
We booked a vacation package that included flights and hotel.

senses.def: to put something into a box or wrapping for sale or transport
examples: The cookies are packaged in recyclable boxes.

note: In American English, package is the usual word for a parcel sent by mail.

senses.def: a small paper or plastic container for food or other goods
examples: Add a packet of sugar to your coffee.
The seed packet says to plant them in spring.

senses.def: a set of documents given to someone
examples: New students receive an information packet on the first day.

note: Americans say "a pack of cigarettes" or "a bag of chips" where British people say "packet".

senses.def: a thick piece of soft material used to protect something, clean something or absorb liquid
examples: Hockey players wear knee pads and shoulder pads.
Clean the wound with a cotton pad.

senses.def: a number of sheets of paper fastened together at one edge
examples: She wrote the number down on a notepad by the phone.

senses.def: (informal) the place where someone lives
examples: He invited us back to his pad for drinks.

senses.def: one side of a sheet of paper in a book or magazine, or a section of a website
examples: Please open your books to page 42.
Check the company's Facebook page for updates.

senses.def: to call someone using a speaker system or electronic device
examples: The hospital paged the surgeon on duty to come to the emergency room.

note: "Be on the same page" (informal) = agree or understand something in the same way.

senses.def: the unpleasant feeling in your body when you are hurt or sick
examples: I've had a sharp pain in my back since yesterday.
The medicine should help with the pain.

senses.def: mental or emotional suffering
examples: Nothing can ease the pain of losing a child.

senses.def: (informal) a person or thing that is annoying
examples: Filling out these tax forms is such a pain.

note: "Take pains to do something" = make a big effort to do it carefully.

senses.def: causing physical pain
examples: My ankle is still painful after the fall.
The injection was quick but painful.

senses.def: causing emotional pain or difficulty
examples: Their divorce was a long and painful process.
It was painful to watch the team lose so badly.

senses.def: a colored liquid put on surfaces to decorate or protect them
examples: The walls need a fresh coat of paint.
Careful, the paint is still wet.

senses.def: to cover a surface with paint
examples: We're painting the kitchen this weekend.

senses.def: to make a picture using paints
examples: She paints landscapes in her free time.

note: "Paint a picture of" can also mean "describe": "The report paints a grim picture of the economy."

senses.def: an artist who paints pictures
examples: Van Gogh is one of the most famous painters in history.
She's a talented painter who sells her work online.

senses.def: a person whose job is painting buildings, walls and rooms
examples: We hired a painter to do the outside of the house.

senses.def: a picture made with paint
examples: The museum owns several paintings by Monet.
A large painting hung above the fireplace.

senses.def: the activity or art of using paint
examples: She took up painting after she retired.

senses.def: two things of the same kind that are used together
examples: I need a new pair of running shoes.
She lost one of her favorite pair of earrings.

senses.def: an object made of two joined parts
examples: He bought two pairs of jeans and a pair of sunglasses.

senses.def: two people who are together or doing something together
examples: Students will work in pairs for this exercise.

note: Trap: one pair of pants/glasses/scissors is a single object. Say "a pair of jeans", not "a jean".

senses.def: the official home of a king, queen or other ruler
examples: Tourists lined up to visit Topkapı Palace in Istanbul.
The royal family lives in a huge palace.

senses.def: having skin that is lighter than usual because of illness, fear or shock
examples: You look pale. Are you feeling OK?
She went pale when she heard the news.

senses.def: light in color; not strong or bright
examples: He was wearing a pale blue shirt.

senses.def: to seem less important when compared with something else
examples: Our problems pale in comparison to theirs.

note: "Pale in comparison (to/with)" = seem much less important or impressive.

senses.def: the inside surface of your hand between the wrist and the fingers
examples: She held the tiny bird in the palm of her hand.
My palms get sweaty when I'm nervous.

senses.def: a tall tropical tree with no branches and long leaves at the top
examples: The beach was lined with palm trees.

note: The l is silent in American English: /pɑːm/. "Have someone in the palm of your hand" = control them completely.

senses.def: a metal container with a handle, used for cooking food on a stove
examples: Heat some oil in a frying pan and add the onions.
Grease the cake pan before you pour in the batter.

senses.def: (informal) to criticize something very strongly
examples: Critics panned the movie, but audiences loved it.

note: "Pan out" (informal) = develop or turn out ("Let's see how things pan out").

senses.def: a flat, usually rectangular piece of wood, glass or metal that forms part of a surface
examples: They installed solar panels on the roof.
The door has a glass panel at the top.

senses.def: a group of people chosen to discuss something, give advice or make decisions
examples: A panel of experts will judge the competition.
She spoke on a panel about women in business.

senses.def: a flat board with controls or instruments on it
examples: The pilot checked the instrument panel.

senses.def: a sudden strong feeling of fear that stops you thinking clearly
examples: There was panic in the streets when the earthquake hit.
She woke up in a panic, sure she had missed her flight.

senses.def: to suddenly feel so afraid that you cannot think clearly
examples: Don't panic; we still have plenty of time.
He panicked when he realized his wallet was gone.

note: Spelling: panicked, panicking (add k before -ed/-ing).

senses.def: a piece of clothing that covers the body from the waist to the ankles, with a part for each leg
examples: I spilled coffee on my new pants.
He wore black pants and a white shirt to the interview.

senses.def: (British) underpants or women's underwear
examples: The little boy fell in a puddle and had to change his pants and socks.

note: American pants = British trousers; British pants = American underwear. Always plural: "These pants are too long."

senses.def: the thin material used for writing, printing and wrapping
examples: Can you give me a piece of paper and a pen?
The printer is out of paper.

senses.def: a newspaper
examples: Did you read the story in today's paper?

senses.def: a piece of academic writing, or an essay written by a student
examples: I have to write a ten-page paper on the Civil War.
She presented a paper at the conference.

senses.def: (plural) official documents
examples: The police officer asked to see his papers.

note: Uncountable for the material (some paper, a piece of paper); countable for a newspaper or essay (a paper). "On paper" = in theory.

senses.def: a public celebration in which people, bands and decorated vehicles move through the streets
examples: Thousands of people watched the Fourth of July parade.
The team celebrated their championship with a parade downtown.

senses.def: to walk somewhere in a public way to be seen, or to show something off
examples: Models paraded down the runway in the new designs.

note: "Rain on someone's parade" (informal) = spoil someone's happy moment.

senses.def: a section of a piece of writing, usually several sentences about one idea, starting on a new line
examples: Your essay should have at least five paragraphs.
The key information is in the second paragraph of the contract.

note: In formal writing, "see paragraph 4" is often written "see para. 4".

senses.def: (of lines) side by side and always the same distance apart
examples: The railroad runs parallel to the river.
Draw two parallel lines across the page.

senses.def: similar, or happening at the same time
examples: The two companies ran parallel investigations.

senses.def: a person, event or situation that is very similar to another
examples: Historians have drawn parallels between the two wars.
This crisis has no parallel in modern history.

note: Spelling: one r, double l, single l at the end. "Unparalleled" = better or greater than any other.

senses.def: a fact or limit that decides how something can be done
examples: We need to work within the parameters of the budget.
The committee set clear parameters for the research.

senses.def: a value in a calculation or program that can be changed
examples: You can adjust the parameters in the settings menu.

note: Usually plural and formal. Don't confuse with perimeter (the outer edge of an area).

senses.def: a person's mother or father
examples: My parents live in a small town in Oregon.
Being a single parent is hard work.

senses.def: an organization that owns smaller companies
examples: The airline's parent company reported record profits.

note: Trap: parents means mother and father only, not relatives in general (akraba = relatives).

senses.def: connected with a parent or parents
examples: Children under 13 need parental permission to join the site.
The phone has parental controls to block certain apps.

note: Note the stress shift: PARent, paRENTal.

senses.def: an area with its own church and priest, or the people who live there
examples: The parish raised money to repair the church roof.
She has been the parish priest for twenty years.

senses.def: in the US state of Louisiana, an area of local government, like a county
examples: Flooding hit several parishes in southern Louisiana.

senses.def: a public area of grass and trees in a town where people walk, play and relax
examples: We took the kids to the park after lunch.
Central Park is crowded on sunny weekends.

senses.def: a large area of land kept for a special purpose, such as nature or business
examples: Yellowstone was the first national park in the US.

senses.def: to leave a vehicle in a place for a period of time
examples: You can't park here; it's a fire lane.

note: "Car park" is British; Americans say "parking lot" or "parking garage".

senses.def: the act of leaving a vehicle somewhere, or space where vehicles can be left
examples: Parking is free after 6 p.m.
It's hard to find parking downtown on Saturdays.

note: Trap: in English, "parking" is not a place; say "parking lot" (otopark), not "a parking".

senses.def: the group of elected people who make and change the laws of a country
examples: The new law was approved by parliament last week.
She was elected to the Turkish parliament in 2018.

note: Pronounced /ˈpɑːrləmənt/; the i is silent. The US equivalent is Congress.

senses.def: connected with a parliament, or having a parliament
examples: Parliamentary elections will be held in the spring.
The country has a parliamentary system of government.

senses.def: some but not all of something, or a piece of a larger whole
examples: The first part of the movie was boring.
We need to replace a broken part in the washing machine.

senses.def: a role in a play or film, or someone's share in an activity
examples: She got the main part in the school play.
Everyone played a part in the team's success.

senses.def: to separate, or to leave someone
examples: They parted as friends after the divorce.

note: "Take part in" = participate (katılmak). "For the most part" = mostly. "Part with something" = give it away unwillingly.

senses.def: for only part of the normal working day or week
examples: She has a part-time job at a bookstore while she studies.
Part-time workers often don't get health insurance.

senses.def: for only part of the working day or week
examples: He works part-time so he can look after his kids.

note: Opposite: full-time. Hyphenated before a noun (a part-time job).

senses.def: not complete or whole
examples: The project was only a partial success.
We received a partial refund for the canceled trip.

senses.def: liking something very much
examples: I'm partial to a cup of hot chocolate in the evening.

senses.def: unfairly supporting one side; biased
examples: The referee was accused of being partial.

note: "Be partial to" (informal) = like. Impartial = fair, not biased (tarafsız).

senses.def: not completely; to some degree
examples: The road is partially closed for repairs.
His face was partially hidden by a hat.

note: Very similar to partly; partially is slightly more formal and common for physical states (partially sighted).

senses.def: a person who takes part in an activity or event
examples: All participants received a certificate at the end of the course.
The study had over 500 participants.

senses.def: to take part in or become involved in an activity
examples: Everyone is encouraged to participate in the discussion.
Over 2,000 runners participated in the marathon.

note: Use IN: participate in something. Trap: "I participate in your opinion" is not English; say "I share your opinion" or "I agree".

senses.def: the act of taking part in an activity or event
examples: Class participation counts for 20% of your grade.
Voter participation was higher than expected.

senses.def: used to show that you mean one specific person or thing and not others
examples: Is there a particular reason you want to leave?
This particular model is no longer available.

senses.def: very careful about choosing exactly what you like; fussy
examples: My cat is very particular about her food.

note: "In particular" = especially. Trap: particular does not mean "private" (özel ders = private lesson).

senses.def: especially; more than usual or more than others
examples: The museum is particularly popular with families.
I didn't particularly enjoy the concert.

note: "Not particularly" = not very (a soft way to say no).

senses.def: to some degree; not completely
examples: The accident was partly my fault.
Tomorrow will be partly cloudy with a chance of rain.

note: "Partly because ... and partly because ..." is a common way to give two reasons.

senses.def: the person you are married to or living with in a romantic relationship
examples: You're welcome to bring your partner to the party.
She lives with her partner and their two kids.

senses.def: one of the owners of a business, or a person or country you work with
examples: He became a partner at the law firm last year.
China is one of the country's main trading partners.

senses.def: a person you do an activity with, such as dancing or a game
examples: Choose a partner for the next exercise.

senses.def: a relationship in which people or organizations work together or share a business
examples: The university formed a partnership with local hospitals.
They went into partnership and opened a bakery.

senses.def: a social event where people eat, drink, talk and enjoy themselves
examples: We're having a party on Saturday for my birthday.
The party went on until 2 a.m.

senses.def: a political organization that tries to win elections
examples: Which party did you vote for in the last election?

senses.def: a group of people doing something together, or one side in a legal agreement or dispute
examples: Both parties signed the contract.
A search party was sent to look for the missing hikers.

note: "Throw/have a party" = organize one. "A third party" = someone not directly involved (üçüncü şahıs).

senses.def: to move past or through something
examples: We passed a gas station a few miles back.
Time passes quickly when you're having fun.

senses.def: to succeed in an exam or test
examples: Did you pass your driving test?

senses.def: to give something to someone, or to officially approve a law
examples: Could you pass the salt, please?
Congress passed the bill by a narrow margin.

senses.def: an official document or ticket that lets you enter a place or travel
examples: Visitors must show their pass at the gate.

note: Trap: "pass an exam" = succeed; "take an exam" = sit it (sınava girmek). "Pass away" = die (polite).

senses.def: a long narrow way that connects one place or room with another
examples: A narrow passage led from the kitchen to the garden.
The secret passage was hidden behind a bookcase.

senses.def: a short section of a book, speech or piece of music
examples: Read the passage and answer the questions below.

senses.def: the process of time passing, or the act of moving through or past something
examples: With the passage of time, the pain became easier to bear.
The bill's passage through Congress took months.

note: "A rite of passage" = an event that marks an important stage in life (graduation, first job).

senses.def: a person traveling in a vehicle who is not driving it or working on it
examples: The plane was carrying 180 passengers and six crew members.
She sat in the passenger seat while her dad drove.

senses.def: the process of time going by
examples: With the passing of the years, the town grew into a city.

senses.def: a polite word for someone's death, or the end of something
examples: We were sad to hear of your grandmother's passing.

senses.def: lasting only a short time, or going past
examples: For him, skateboarding was just a passing phase.
She waved at a passing car.

note: "Mention something in passing" = mention it briefly while talking about something else (laf arasında).
